title: CHAPTER EIGHTEEN. Sanctification and good works: definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM OCTAVUM, De sanctificatione et bonis operibus. Sanctificatio sive renovatio fidelium et BONA OPERA sunt actiones hominum conversorum per operationem Spiritus Sancti ex vera fide secundum normam legis divinae praestitae, quibus singulis momentis in ipsis peccatum mortificatur et imago Dei renovatur ad obedientiam atque honorem Deo deferendum. Renovatio a regeneratione differt: per regenerationem filii Dei efficimur; per renovationem filii Dei declaramur. Illa mutatio status; haec qualitatum.
english: CHAPTER EIGHTEEN. On sanctification and good works.

Sanctification or renewal of believers and GOOD WORKS are actions of the converted performed by the Holy Spirit's operation from true faith according to the norm of divine law, by which moment by moment sin is mortified in them and God's image renewed unto obedience and honor to God.
Renewal differs from regeneration: by regeneration we are made God's children; by renewal we are declared such. The one changes state; the other qualities.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Renewal differs from regeneration: by regeneration we stand as made God's children; by renewal we stand as declared such. Ye one changes state; ye other qualities. — Sanctification or renewal belonging toward believers and GOOD WORKS stand as actions belonging toward ye converted performed by ye Holy Spirit's operation from true faith according toward ye norm belonging toward divine law, by which moment by moment sin stands as mortified in them and God's image renewed unto obedience and honor toward God. — CHAPTER EIGHTEEN. On sanctification and good works.

title: Causes: Spirit principal; faith secondary; form = conformity to law
latin: Efficiens principalis est Spiritus Sanctus (Rom. 8:14; Ezek. 36:26-27). Proxima et secundaria causa est vera fides per charitatem efficax (Gal. 5:6). Forma bonorum operum posita est in congruentia cum lege Dei—peccatum est anomia, bonum opus isonomia. Quia tamen opera fidelium imperfecta sunt, per fidem in Christum defectus supplentur et Christus fide apprehensus suam iustitiam nostram facit, ut opera Deo placeant (Gen. 4:4; Heb. 11:4).
english: The principal efficient cause is the Holy Spirit; the proximate secondary cause is true faith working through love.

The form of good works lies in conformity to God's law—sin is lawlessness, a good work is law-keeping. Yet because believers' works are imperfect, defects are supplied through faith in Christ, and Christ apprehended by faith makes His righteousness ours so that the works please God.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye form belonging toward good works lies in conformity toward God's law—sin stands as lawlessness, a good work stands as law-keeping. Yet because believers' works stand as imperfect, defects stand as supplied through faith in Christ, and Christ apprehended by faith makes His righteousness ours so that ye works please God. — Ye principal efficient cause stands as ye Holy Spirit; ye proximate secondary cause stands as true faith working through love.

title: Ends: God, self, neighbor; necessity of good works
latin: Fines: propter Deum obedientia et honor; propter nos ipsos ut vocationem confirmemus; propter proximum ut charitatis officiis sublevemus nec scandala simus. De necessitate: bona opera non sunt necessaria ad iustificationem tanquam causa, sed necessaria sunt in iustificatis tanquam fructus et via vitae Christianae—contra Pontificios qui ea in iustificationem ingerunt.
english: Ends: toward God—obedience and honor; toward ourselves—confirming our calling; toward the neighbor—relieving by love's duties and avoiding scandal.

On necessity: good works are not necessary to justification as a cause, but are necessary in the justified as fruit and the Christian way of life—against those who thrust them into justification itself.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): On necessity: good works stand as not necessary toward justification as a cause, but stand as necessary in ye justified as fruit and ye Christian way belonging toward life—against those who thrust them into justification itself. — Ends: toward God—obedience and honor; toward ourselves—confirming our calling; toward ye neighbor—relieving by love's duties and avoiding scandal.

title: Perfection and imperfection of saints' works
latin: VII. De perfectione: asserimus bona sanctorum opera in hac vita non esse perfecta ad mensuram legis. VIII. Ea imperfectio frequentissime ratione partium, semper vero ratione graduum. Opus est quotidiana remissione; nemo prior dedit Deo ut retribuatur ei. Meritum condignum et congruum repudiandum; Deus coronat in nobis sua dona, non nostra merita (Augustine).
english: VII–VIII. On perfection: we assert that the saints' good works in this life are not perfect by the law's measure. That imperfection appears often as to parts, always as to degrees.
Daily remission is needed; no one first gave to God so as to be repaid. Condign and congruent merit are to be rejected; God crowns His own gifts in us, not our merits.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Daily remission stands as needed; no one first gave toward God so as toward be repaid. Condign and congruent merit stand as toward be rejected; God crowns His own gifts in us, not our merits. — VII–VIII. On perfection: we assert that ye saints' good works in this life stand as not perfect by ye law's measure. That imperfection appears often as toward parts, always as toward degrees.

title: Notabilia: self-denial; law as canon; Cap.19 next
latin: 1. Bonorum operum studium necessario includit sui ipsius abnegationem et crucis tolerantiam. 2. Quae Christianis facienda sint, lex Dei perfecte ostendit tanquam divina regula et canon; Christus exemplar. Sine vera Dei notitia ferri nequeunt. CAPUT DECIMUM NONUM sequitur, De libertate Christiana.
english: 1. Zeal for good works necessarily includes self-denial and bearing the cross. 2. What Christians must do, God's law perfectly shows as divine rule and canon; Christ is the pattern. Without true knowledge of God they cannot be borne.
CHAPTER NINETEEN follows, On Christian liberty.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER NINETEEN follows, On Christian liberty. — 1. Zeal for good works necessarily includes self-denial and bearing ye cross. 2. What Christians must do, God's law perfectly shows as divine rule and canon; Christ stands as ye pattern. Without true knowledge belonging toward God they cannot be borne.
